outline.h2: Why Do Bay Area Floors Sag in the First Place?
outline.notes: Question-form H2. outline.h2: Sister-Joist Repair ($2,500–$8,000)
outline.notes: When it's the right fix: bouncy/sagging in a specific room, joists are undersized or have end rot, framing is otherwise sound. Process: temporary shoring, cut back rotted ends, bolt new 2x10 or 2x12 alongside existing. Common on Noe Valley Victorians, Alameda Edwardians, Berkeley bungalows.

outline.h2: Full Joist or Beam Replacement ($6,000–$18,000)
outline.notes: When it's the right fix: multiple joists compromised, central beam is sagging or notched, prior sister attempts failed. Process: expose structure, temporary shoring, remove damaged members, install new LVL or steel beam, re-attach joists. More common on multi-flat Victorians and Mission flats with carved-up basements.

outline.h2: Sagging From Foundation Settlement ($12,000–$25,000+)
outline.notes: Important caveat — this is where symptoms overlap with foundation movement. Signs: stair-step cracks in stucco, doors sticking, slope that follows the whole floor plan, not just one bay. The fix is NOT underpinning (Gadget doesn't sell that). The fix is level/correct what's accessible — rebuild sill plates, replace rotted framing above the foundation, level floors with new sistered joists at correct elevation. Reference Earthquake Brace + Bolt program by name for the common seismic retrofit combo.
